faqs.answer: Lemon-dressed asparagus, grilled corn, and a simple green salad. Grilled salmon wants sides from the same grill or a bright, acidic salad — nothing heavy or creamy.

faqs.answer: Lemon herb rice, roasted baby potatoes, shaved fennel and orange salad, and garlic butter green beans. Baked salmon is gentle, so the sides can be warm and earthy.

faqs.answer: Miso-glazed eggplant, sesame spinach, and steamed rice. Teriyaki is sweet and salty, so the sides should be savoury and light rather than sweet.
faqs.question: What goes with teriyaki salmon?

faqs.answer: About 4–6 oz per adult for a main course — a standard fillet. For 8 guests, plan on about 2½ pounds of fillets.

body: Salmon is rich in its own right — oily, full-flavoured, and quick to cook. That richness is the whole pairing problem: a creamy or heavy side doubles it, and the plate feels fatty. The best sides are bright and fresh for rich preparations, or warm and earthy for lighter ones. Pick a cooking method and the sides follow — a grilled fillet and a teriyaki fillet do not want the same plate.
sections.callout: Salmon needs acid the way steak needs salt. Lemon, asparagus, a vinaigrette salad — one sharp element per plate, minimum.

body: Salmon's sides depend on how it is cooked. A grilled fillet has char and smoke, so it wants sweet corn and slaw. A baked fillet is gentle, so it takes warm, earthy sides. Teriyaki is sweet and salty, so its sides should be savoury and light. Pan-seared salmon has a crisp crust, so it wants something soft and saucy underneath.

body: Salmon is a dinner-party main because it cooks in minutes and scales by fillet. Plan 4–6 oz per adult — a standard fillet each — and ¾ cup of each side per person. For 8 guests that is about 2½ pounds of fillets, 6 cups of rice, 6 cups of roasted vegetables, and 8 cups of salad. Cook the salmon last: it waits badly, and the sides hold.

body: A few combinations fight the salmon instead of helping it. Skip a second rich, oily fish preparation — salmon with a creamy seafood pasta is richness doubled. Skip a strongly spiced side that buries the fish's own flavour; salmon is delicate, and a heavy curry or chilli sauce wins the fight. And skip a sweet glaze on the side when the salmon already has one — teriyaki with honey-glazed carrots is sugar on sugar.
bullets: No second rich seafood main — one fish per plate.

body: Salmon is done at 145°F internal temperature, with a few minutes of rest — the flesh should flake easily but still be slightly translucent in the centre. That is done, not raw. Keep cooked salmon above 140°F while serving and refrigerate leftovers within two hours (one hour above 90°F). Leftover salmon is best eaten cold the next day, flaked into salad, rather than reheated until dry.
